statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress of 68% (high) while the Strait of Hormuz stays closed on Iran's seven stated conditions, four vessels were struck between 1 and 4 October, and a Tehran source describes preparations for a major round of fighting.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, 00:00-02:00 Berlin on 5 October, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on weekend-gap and thin-liquidity grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this state.
headline: Hormuz stays shut on Iran's seven conditions while Tail holds its halt-session floor three hours before the 22:00Z CME reopen
body:
CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor of 3%. The last observed structure was orderly and two-way: the cash index set a record intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, surrendered it in full, and closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00% from a 30,501.60 previous close, in the lower half of its 30,737.07-31,017.53 range. December NQ futures settled at 31,049, up 0.94%, which is the reference for any weekend gap. A record close that gives back its own high is the opposite of the no-retracement path Tail is designed to measure.

Cross-assets conflict rather than align, which under this contract raises Stress and uncertainty instead of Tail. September payrolls rose 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, and October Fed hike odds fell to roughly 17% from about 36% a week earlier, yet the 2-year yield still ended Friday up 5.0 basis points at 4.837% and the 10-year up 4.5 basis points at 5.279% after an initial fall. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October shows the 2-year at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%. VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31, near its session low, while WTI eased 1.90% to $91.11 and Brent sat near $102.25 after the G7 announced the release of 100 million barrels of crude and diesel reserves over four months. Low volatility and softer oil alongside rising yields is a mixed configuration, not a directional one.

The Strait of Hormuz remains the dominant Stress driver and is unresolved on both tracks. Iran's parliament speaker restated that the waterway stays closed until seven conditions tied to the June Islamabad memorandum are met; Tehran is reviewing the US response to its seven-day reopening proposal while public talks are stalled and Qatari backchannel contact is reported. UKMTO documented four tanker strikes in the strait between 1 and 4 October, transits have been suppressed to single digits against a pre-crisis baseline near 85 per day, and roughly 218 vessels are anchored outside the crisis zone. A tanker reported explosions south of Al Mukha and explosions were heard near Qeshm and Sirik, with no confirmed land impacts. A Tehran source describes preparations for a major round of fighting, and a third US carrier strike group has deployed. Stress is held at 68% in the high band on that evidence; it does not by itself establish a pathological Nasdaq-100 price path.

The published forecast therefore holds Tail between 3% and 9% through the remaining closed hours and raises it to 22% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z reopen and the hour after it, where a weekend gap into the thinnest book of the week is the one genuine mean-reversion hazard in this horizon. That window is published as the danger window. Tail then decays through the Asian and European sessions and rebuilds modestly to a 17% peak at the 14:00Z ISM Services PMI on 5 October, the week's first high-impact US release, which is scored as a catalyst rather than an automatic block because no post-release path is observable at the assessment cutoff. Shared Finviz context was present but carried a 29 September collection time and partial status, so it was treated as stale and excluded from this assessment, which rests on independent current research.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 3% in every slot, with every hour mapping to EA_ON and green and the dominant mode normal throughout, reflecting a market that was either in orderly two-way trade or closed. Stress rose from 64% at 19:00Z on 3 October to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October as the weekend Hormuz checkpoints opened, then eased through the 73%, 70%, 68% and 66% readings of the European and early US-equivalent hours to settle in a 64% to 68% band. Confidence ran between 83% and 88%, improving through the Sunday hours as current levels, yields, oil and the forward calendar were re-verified while the live price path stayed structurally unavailable inside the weekend halt.
outlookSummary: The remaining closed Sunday hours carry no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held at 3% and 4% through 20:00Z while Stress stays near 68% on the closed strait and the stalled public talks. Tail then steps to 9% in the final closed hour and is raised to 22% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, which the published danger window covers; that step reflects weekend-gap and thin-liquidity hazard, not observed one-way structure, and an early orderly retracement would invalidate it. Tail then decays to a 7% to 9% range through the Asian and European sessions, rebuilds to 11% and 15% into the US pre-market and the 13:30Z cash open, peaks at 17% for the 14:00Z ISM Services PMI, and eases back to 10% by the final published hour. Stress trends down from 70% at the reopen to 60% by the end of the horizon, and every forecast hour outside the two reopen slots maps to EA_ON and green.
